12. Describe the measures taken by the entity to ensure a safe and healthy workplace.
 The Company prioritises a “Zero Harm” and “Safety First” culture and remains firmly committed to this mission, which is 
further reinforced through initiatives such as “Zero Accident / Zero Illness” campaigns and safety week/month celebrations. 
Safety performance and improvement initiatives across each plant are reviewed on a monthly basis by the Managing Director 
and periodically by the Board, ensuring strong governance and oversight. Key leading indicators, such as near misses and 
unsafe acts, are monitored and communicated by digital safety reporting systems, with a continued emphasis on proactive risk 
identification and mitigation.
 The Company has implemented a VSL programme, which is driven by the leadership and includes safety through active shop-
floor engagement, proactive identification of hazards, coaching employees on safe behaviours, and reinforcement of safety 
standards. To further strengthen safety governance, the Company has institutionalised the role of Safety Champions across 
departments for the review and closure of safety findings. In addition, Night Duty Officers are appointed across facilities to 
ensure continuous monitoring and safety compliance during night shifts. The Company’s Health and Safety framework and 
Management System encompass the following:
	 Policies and Guidelines: The Company’s Safety Policy incorporates detailed commitments, accountability, and process 
requirements. A key focus area during the reporting year was the standardisation of the HIRA framework across all plants 
through a common template, uniform risk rating criteria, and consistent application of the hierarchy of controls.
	 Training and Simulations on Health, Safety, and Work Environment: All employees, workers, and contractors undergo 
structured induction, job-specific, specialised, and on-the-job safety training, including HIRA implementation. Regular 
mock drills covering fire, evacuation, and emergency response are conducted to enhance preparedness. 
	 Safety Equipment and Awareness: Safety awareness is reinforced through shift meetings, toolbox talks, signage, digital 
communication, and engagement initiatives such as safety quizzes and campaigns. Strict adherence to Personal Protective 
Equipment (PPE) usage, alongside permit-to-work systems and critical safety protocols. Implementation of 5S and Kaizen 
practices supports workplace cleanliness and organisation. 
	 Safety at Workplace: All plants have Safety Committees with worker representation, in line with the Factories Act. 
These committees review hazards, validate corrective actions, and monitor their timely closure. Safety Champions and 
Night Duty Officers strengthen on-ground safety awareness. Machine safety is ensured through systematic identification 
of hazards and implementation of control measures to ensure safe operation of machinery and equipment, including 
installation of emergency stops, interlocks, and enhanced guarding mechanisms in line with safety standards. Behavioural 
safety programmes are implemented to promote safe practices and reinforce a culture of safety across the workforce. 
Regular hygiene and sanitation audits are conducted across canteens, shopfloors, and washrooms, with supporting 
systems for pest control and waste management. Periodic checks are also carried out to ensure drinking water quality, 
while shopfloor conditions are maintained through adequate ventilation and temperature control. The Company has 
established comprehensive occupational health measures, including fully equipped Occupational Health Centres (OHCs) 
38  
|Endurance Technologies Limited
=== page 309 ===
and maintenance of employee health records. Periodic and pre-employment medical check-ups are conducted, with a 
special focus on high-risk exposures such as dust, chemicals, and noise. Emergency preparedness is further strengthened 
through ambulance tie-ups and access to nearby hospitals, ensuring timely medical response.
	 Rewards and Recognition: As part of its continuous improvement approach, plant teams proactively identify opportunities 
to enhance safety performance and implement initiatives such as Kaizen to drive incremental improvements. The Company 
promotes the sharing of safety-related knowledge and best practices across locations and reinforces this by recognising 
safety leaders through Safety Champion Rounds, which also serve as a platform for knowledge sharing and the adoption 
of best practices.
	 Wellness: The Company promotes employee well-being through initiatives such as Sports Fest 2026, featuring competitions 
in cricket, volleyball, badminton, table tennis, chess, carrom, and a women’s cricket tournament. Additionally, the “Mindful 
Beginnings” programme supports mental well-being by fostering calmness, positivity, and a healthier workplace culture.

1. Does the entity extend any life insurance or any compensatory package in the event of the death of (A) Employees (Y/N) 
(B) Workers (Y/N). 
 Yes. The Company provides life insurance and compensatory coverage to both employees and workers through Group Personal 
Accident (GPA) and Mediclaim insurance policies. In the reporting year, a new term life insurance policy was introduced, 
providing additional coverage for its employees. These initiatives offer financial assistance in the event of accidents, medical 
emergencies, or loss of life. In the unfortunate event of death, eligible family members may also receive benefits under the 
Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) scheme, including coverage under the Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI) scheme 
and, where applicable, funeral benefits through the ESIC. Contract workers are covered under the applicable provisions of ESIC 
and the LWF, in line with statutory requirements.
2. Provide the measures undertaken by the entity to ensure that statutory dues have been deducted and deposited by the 
value chain partners.
 The Company has instituted a structured and contractually enforced compliance framework to ensure that statutory dues are 
deducted and deposited by its contractual labour providers in accordance with the provisions of the Contract Labour Act. All 
service agreements incorporate clearly defined obligations related to the timely payment of wages and deposit of statutory 
dues, including PF, ESIC, and applicable taxes such as Goods and Services Tax (GST). A mutually agreed compliance and 
penalty mechanism is embedded within these contracts, and instances of short payment, part payment, or delayed remittance 
trigger defined financial penalties, with stricter consequences for repeat non-compliances that could include potential 
contract termination.
 To ensure effective implementation, the Company has established a multi-layered verification and monitoring system. Vendor 
invoices are processed only after validation of statutory payment proofs, including reconciliation of PF contributions with 
Universal Account Number (UAN) records to verify deposits. Wage payments are further validated for minimum wages and 
other statutory requirements through Permanent Account Number (PAN) and Aadhaar-linked records to ensure transparency 
and traceability. The Company also undertakes ongoing engagement and periodic reviews with contractual labour providers, 
along with continuous monitoring and tracking mechanisms, to drive sustained compliance with applicable regulations. All 
supplier agreements, including those with labour service providers, contain provisions requiring compliance with applicable 
statutory regulations. In addition, the Company’s VCOC requires suppliers to provide self-declarations confirming adherence 
to statutory obligations, which are periodically audited. These audits are conducted in line with a prioritised audit plan to 
strengthen compliance across the supply chain.

 Note: The Company has a robust assessment protocol covering both health and safety as well as working conditions of its 
suppliers across the OEM and aftermarket businesses. The foundation is a safety systems evaluation, including compliance, role

requirements, including Fire No Objection Certificate (NOC), use of PPEs, fire protection systems, emergency exits and assembly

such as ventilation, daylight, and fume extraction and safety practices, including mock drills and functioning of safety committees, 
are a part of the process. Suppliers that use processes with greater safety risk in their operations are assessed more frequently 
with an emphasis on identifying risks and training needs. For the aftermarket suppliers as well, quality teams conduct system

houses and professional service providers whose engagements are intermittent in nature and, therefore, are currently outside

6. Provide details of any corrective actions taken or underway to address significant risks / concerns arising from assessments 
of health and safety practices and working conditions of value chain partners. 
 The Company’s approach is to move beyond basic compliance and support its suppliers in building continuous improvement 
systems. Progressively enhanced standards help define potential risks proactively, and the Company uses a combination of 
assessments, corrective action plans and training programmes to elevate performance.  
 In FY 2025-26, the Company conducted 132 audits, which focused on specific aspects, including fire and electrical safety systems, 
to drive continuous improvement. In addition, some process-specific suppliers, for example, shot blasting, have been identified 
for enhanced scrutiny.  Suppliers are encouraged to upgrade safety infrastructure and systems, including fire extinguishers, 
sprinkler systems, and fire hydrants. For shot blasting operations, wet scrubbers were installed to improve safety and control 
emissions. Additional measures included improving safety practices in areas such as paint booths through appropriate PPE 
usage, along with training on fire extinguisher use, fire mock drills, Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), and ensuring periodic 
occupational health assessments. These themes are monitored and recommended as part of the supplier improvement plans.

Leadership Indicators
1. Provide the processes for consultation between stakeholders and the Board on economic, environmental, and social 
topics, or if consultation is delegated, how is feedback from such consultations provided to the Board? 
 The Company’s ESG governance framework incorporates structured processes for stakeholder engagement through periodic 
consultations, reviews and monitoring engagement platforms to ensure responsiveness and collaborative partnering. The Board 
has delegated the responsibility of stakeholder engagement to the Management, which also consists of functional leaders 
who are responsible for engaging with relevant stakeholders on environmental, social, and economic matters, as described 
under Principle 4, Essential Indicator 2. Any grievances are addressed promptly through structured mechanisms with defined 
accountabilities. Feedback received through these channels is reviewed by the ESG Council (chaired by the Executive Directors) 
to drive continuous improvement and recommend corrective actions, including systemic and process change if necessary.
 At the Board level, the RMC provides oversight on ESG-related matters. During its half-yearly review meetings, the Committee 
assesses ESG risks, their mitigation measures wherever required, as well as progress on addressing ESG opportunities, 
considering insights from stakeholder consultations. In addition, specific stakeholder inputs are considered through dedicated 
Board-constituted Committees. Matters raised by investors and shareholders are addressed by the Stakeholder Relationship 
Committee, while feedback from local communities is reviewed by the CSR Committee. Key updates on stakeholder concerns 
and the Company’s responses are also shared periodically with the Board by these committees. Board discussions with executive 
leadership provide platforms for incorporating stakeholder inputs, ensuring that the Board remains informed while making 
decisions on economic, environmental, and social matters. In this regard, the Board has also approved an ESG Charter, which 
serves as a guiding framework for the Company’s focus on sustainable and responsible business practices. The said Charter is 
available on the website of the Company at https://www.endurancegroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Environmental-
Social-and-Governance-Charter.pdf.  
2. Whether stakeholder consultation is used to support the identification and management of environmental, and social 
topics (Yes / No). If so, provide details of instances as to how the inputs received from stakeholders on these topics were 
incorporated into the policies and activities of the entity. 
 Yes, stakeholder consultation is actively leveraged by various functional teams to identify and manage environmental and social topics, 
helping define the Company’s material ESG priorities and guiding resource allocation to effectively integrate feedback into policies 
and operations. Inputs from employees have been incorporated through initiatives such as the introduction of term life insurance 
and the digitisation of the WOW recognition programme via an online platform. Feedback from workers has been incorporated into 
improved welfare measures, including the provision of automated roti makers and subsidised, nutritious meals in canteens. 
44  
|Endurance Technologies Limited
=== page 315 ===
 A key supplier concern addressed during the year was around vehicle turnaround times. Actions taken include enabling advance 
shipment notice through the vendor portal, aggregation of multi-part suppliers into single invoices, allocation of dedicated 
delivery time windows and an increase in the number of delivery bays. To improve transparency and align quality performance, 
the Company has digitised the count of delivery lots needing segregation to support suppliers in monitoring and improving 
performance.  During the EVA meetings, the need for capability upgradation was highlighted; accordingly, targeted training 
sessions were organised on IoT and auto-ballooning software. Separately, in line with the increased focus on building a green 
supply chain, dedicated training sessions on environmental sustainability were conducted by external and internal subject matter 
experts to strengthen suppliers’ awareness and adoption of sustainable practices. Several VAVE projects were executed in 
collaboration with suppliers across product categories. Similarly, ongoing engagement with OEMs through satisfaction surveys, 
value engineering programmes, and close collaboration with the R&D and quality teams ensures that feedback is systematically 
incorporated into existing and new product development, while also strengthening internal processes and supplier quality 
management systems. Monthly quality performance data from customers is analysed and leveraged to drive continuous 
improvement programs, which are then horizontally deployed across all the plants.  
 Feedback from dealers, retailers and mechanics has led to the Company launching the ‘Endurance Saathi App’ to provide 
greater engagement and the deployment of a digital loyalty program. A key feature includes the implementation of an instant 
payout mechanism enabled through a payment gateway. Retailers can scan product QR codes to validate their authenticity 
and review product information on the App and place orders. The Company has also initiated a stronger quality monitoring 
mechanism at its warehouses before dispatch to dealers to minimise the occurrence of defects and product returns. Additionally, 
features such as stickers for easy identification of bike-specific parts have been added to the packaging. The field sales team 
has been strengthened for market outreach initiatives to support long-term channel partners in creating product awareness 
among retailers and mechanics in their markets. These initiatives also help encourage adoption of the application and loyalty 
programme. Additionally, the Company expanded its aftermarket portfolio during FY 2025–26 with the introduction of products 
such as CVT pulleys, green bushes, link bushes, brake fluid, Bendix components, brake drums, and alloy wheels based on 
dealer feedback. 
3. Provide details of instances of engagement with, and actions taken to address the concerns of vulnerable/marginalised 
stakeholder groups. 
The Company continues to engage with vulnerable and marginalised stakeholder groups through its CSR initiatives, with a focus 
on addressing evolving community needs based on regular feedback and on-ground assessments.
Building on inputs from beneficiaries of the Mobile Medical Clinic initiative, the Company strengthened its healthcare interventions 
by introducing focused programmes targeting anaemia, hypertension, and diabetes. Anaemia screening and treatment are 
primarily directed at female beneficiaries aged 11 years and above. Blood pressure and diabetes screenings are conducted 
for individuals aged 40 years and above. Individuals identified as borderline diabetic undergo further diagnostic evaluation. 
Based on diagnosis, necessary medication is prescribed, and the first dose is administered on-site to ensure immediate care. 
To address livelihood-related concerns, the Company expanded its vocational training initiatives. A new course in ‘Hospitality’ 
has been introduced, aligned with the growing number of hotels in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and the resulting employment 
opportunities. The programme primarily supports school dropouts and individuals from economically disadvantaged households 
by enhancing their employability.
In response to heavy rainfall and flooding in certain areas of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, the Company provided immediate 
relief support. A total of 600 food kits were distributed to affected families. School kits were also provided to children to support 
continuity in education. Additionally, the Company is supporting the development of green cover in the Safari Park, in line with 
the habitat requirements of wildlife relocated from the city zoo. This initiative contributes to ecological restoration and improved 
living conditions for the animals.

4. Do you have a focal point (Individual / Committee) responsible for addressing human rights impacts or issues caused or 
contributed to by the business?  
 Yes. The Company has a Human Rights Committee that acts as the focal point for addressing human rights issues arising from 
its operations. The Committee oversees implementation of the Human Rights Policy, evaluates actual and potential human 
rights risks linked to business activities, and ensures alignment with applicable laws and internationally recognised human rights 
standards. The Company also reviews reported concerns, recommends corrective actions, and facilitates appropriate redressal 
while strengthening processes to prevent recurrence.
 The Human Resources Department supports the Committee through periodic training and awareness programmes. Management 
across all levels remains responsible for ensuring adherence in day-to-day operations. The policy framework also extends to 
sourcing and supply chain activities, requiring compliance from third-party vendors and suppliers. This governance structure 
reflects the Company’s commitment to respecting and safeguarding human rights across its value chain. The Human Rights 
Policy is available at: https://www.endurancegroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/human-rights-policy.pdf. For more details 
on the assessment of suppliers on Human Rights, please refer to Principle 5, Leadership Indicators 4 and 5.

5. Describe the internal mechanisms in place to redress grievances related to human rights issues. 
 The Company has a structured, confidential and secure grievance redressal mechanism to address concerns related to human 
rights. The mechanism is accessible to both internal and external stakeholders and ensures protection against any form of 
retaliation against the complainant. Concerns may also be reported through the procedures specified in the Vigil Mechanism-
cum-Whistle Blower Policy, which is available on the Company’s website. Grievances may also be submitted directly via e-mail 
at etl_governance@endurance.co.in. The Company’s Human Rights Policy is available at: https://www.endurancegroup.com/
wp-content/uploads/2025/07/human-rights-policy.pdf. 
 All reported matters are reviewed under the oversight of the Human Rights Committee. The Committee appoints an 
independent investigation team to examine grievances, assess their validity, and recommend appropriate corrective measures. 
Based on the findings, the Committee works with Senior Management to ensure timely resolution and the implementation of 
preventive actions. The outcomes are communicated to the complainant and relevant functional heads to address potential 
risks and strengthen safeguards. The Company’s VCOC also requires business partners to provide self-declarations confirming 
compliance with human rights requirements. This extends accountability across the value chain. In addition, periodic audits are 
conducted to assess adherence, particularly in areas such as the prevention of child labour, wages, and statutory compliance. 
Further information is provided under Principle 3, Essential Indicator 6.

8. Mechanisms to prevent adverse consequences to the complainant in discrimination and harassment cases.
 The Company is committed to promoting an inclusive and respectful workplace that is free from discrimination and harassment. 
This commitment is reinforced through the ECOC, supported by periodic employee training programmes. It is further strengthened 
by the POSH Policy and the Grievance Redressal Policy. The GRC addresses concerns relating to discrimination, harassment, 
or violations of Company policies, while cases of sexual harassment are handled by the Internal Complaints Committee. The 
Company also has a Vigil Mechanism-cum-Whistleblower Policy in place. This policy safeguards whistleblowers from retaliation 
48  
|Endurance Technologies Limited
=== page 319 ===
or any form of unfair treatment. Protection extends to actions such as discrimination, harassment, victimisation, intimidation, 
or adverse employment decisions. These may include termination, suspension, disciplinary action, transfer, demotion, denial 
of promotion, or other similar measures. The policy also ensures that no authority is used, directly or indirectly, to prevent a 
whistleblower from performing his/her duties or making further protected disclosures. Details regarding employee training on 
POSH and Diversity and Inclusion are provided under Principle 5, Essential Indicator 1.
9. Do human rights requirements form part of your business agreements and contracts?
 Yes. Human rights considerations are incorporated into the Company’s business agreements and contracts. All suppliers, 
vendors, and contractual labour providers are required to self-attest compliance with the Company’s VCOC. The said Code 
incorporates key human rights principles, including non-discrimination, fair wages, and the prohibition of child labour and forced 
labour, among other requirements. In addition, all value chain partners are expected to comply with applicable state and central 
laws governing workforce rights and labour practices. Compliance with these requirements is also reviewed through periodic 
audits. These provisions are embedded within contractual terms to ensure alignment with the Company’s ethical standards and 
legal obligations.

11. Provide details of any corrective actions taken or underway to address significant risks / concerns arising from the 
assessments at Question 10 above.
 The Company has implemented several preventive actions to address any risks and concerns identified through its assessments.  
During the assessment process for providers of contractual labour (detailed in Principle 3, Leadership Indicator 2), certain repeated 
procedural errors leading to compliance misses due to oversight by the vendors were identified. In response, as a proactive 
measure, the Company has organised targeted training and awareness sessions for all vendors to strengthen their understanding of 
applicable requirements and eliminate instances of non-compliance. These initiatives are aimed at ensuring sustained adherence 
to statutory and Company standards across the value chain on social security and related human rights aspects.

1. Details of a business process being modified / introduced as a result of addressing human rights grievances / complaints. 
 The Company has not received any grievances/complaints on human rights issues, excluding those on POSH, as disclosed 
earlier in the report. The Company periodically evaluates its processes to ensure appropriate checks and balances are in place 
and no modifications were found to be necessary.
2. Details of the scope and coverage of any Human rights due diligence conducted. 
 The most significant potential Human Rights risk for the Company is from its contractual workforce. The Company conducts 
due diligence on the deposit of statutory dues with the authorities for social security benefits for the ‘other than permanent’ 
workers across all plants. Details are discussed in Principle 3, Leadership Indicator 4. Based on these human rights assessments 
undertaken, the Company identified trends and organised training sessions for labour contractors to ensure adherence to all 
applicable statutory obligations towards their workforce.

5. Has the entity implemented a mechanism for Zero Liquid Discharge? If yes, provide details of its coverage and 
implementation.  
 Yes, the Company has installed ZLD systems at 11 plants spread across multiple locations in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (3 
Plants), Pune (3 Plants), Chennai, Vallam, Sanand, Narsapura and Halol. These systems help meet regulatory requirements and 
Consent-to-Operate (CTO) conditions. The Company is also assessing the feasibility of extending ZLD to other locations.
 The Company maintains a strong focus on water management as a material priority. It uses STP , ETP , Reverse Osmosis (RO) 
systems, and evaporation systems to treat and reuse water. Treated water is reused in cooling towers, scrubbers, air handling 
units (AHUs), toilet flushing, bin washing, and gardening. RO reject and treated water is also reused for utility and housekeeping 
purposes, reducing the need for fresh water. This focus is further reinforced through the organisation of monthly campaigns on 
water conservation and water flow management across locations. Rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge systems are in 
place to improve water availability and reduce dependence on external sources. Coolant recovery systems help extend coolant

across plants based on current water usage. This has improved measurement, standardised data tracking, and increased visibility 
of water use, enabling identification of leaks, losses, and high-consumption areas. It also supports better planning of water-
saving initiatives and enhances data quality for management review.
 Further details on water management are available on Page 53 of the “Sustainability” section of the Annual Report.

8. Does the entity have any projects related to reducing Green House Gas emission? If yes, then provide details.
 The Board and leadership of the Company recognise climate action and GHG mitigation as key pillars of its ESG strategy. The 
Corporate Sustainability team leads strategic long-term initiatives supporting the Company’s carbon neutrality ambitions. The 
Company continues to invest in the financial, material and human resources required to achieve time-bound goals under its 
ESG roadmap, supported by a plant-level ownership and accountability framework. GHG emissions performance and progress 
on improvement initiatives are monitored and reviewed monthly at the senior-most levels. To accelerate implementation, the 
Company conducts awareness and capability-building programmes to enable rapid horizontal deployment of initiatives across 
facilities. Workshops focused on ideation and improvement opportunities, along with continuous improvement Kaizens, are 
supported through appropriate rewards and recognition programmes. Several new projects were launched during FY 2025–26 
alongside the scale-up of existing programmes across facilities.
	 Net Zero Roadmap: The Company is in the process of developing a Net-Zero Roadmap in line with the SBTi guidelines. 
The roadmap will be anchored on verified Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions data, supplemented by assessed Scope 3 
emissions for applicable categories and insights from product LCAs. This roadmap sets the foundation for the Company’s 
decarbonisation journey and will culminate in the formal submission of SBTi targets, reinforcing its long-term sustainability 
commitments. Key current focus areas include:
	 Energy efficiency improvements across operations.
	 Expansion of renewable energy capacity to reduce dependence on non-renewable sources.
	 Enhanced circularity in material use, promoting re-use, recycling and resource efficiency.
	 Product redesigns guided by carbon hotspot analysis, ensuring targeted emission reductions.
	 Acceleration of Renewable Transition: In addition to the Company’s existing solar and wind assets, a comprehensive 
techno-commercial assessment of renewable energy potential has been undertaken across all facilities. Based on this 
evaluation, solar capacity has been expanded at Company sites, complemented by new group captive arrangements and 
long-term Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) for a reliable supply of green energy. Further, the Company has strengthened 
its renewable portfolio by enhancing its in-house wind power infrastructure, resulting in increased wind energy generation. 
These initiatives enabled the Company to increase the share of renewable energy to 13.98% of total energy consumption 
and 28.08% of electrical energy in FY 2025-26, reinforcing its commitment to transitioning towards clean energy and 
reducing dependence on fossil fuels.
	 Life Cycle Assessments (LCA): As part of its progressive sustainability plan, the Company has undertaken cradle-to-grave 
product LCA for its braking systems, along with four products from the braking division and one product each from the 
castings and transmission divisions. This ensures coverage of at least one representative product from each product family. 
The objective of these assessments is to evaluate process- and product-level environmental impacts, including embodied 
carbon across the lifecycle, enabling informed decision-making for the design and manufacture of more sustainable 
products. Further details of these initiatives are provided under Principle 2, Leadership Indicators 1 and 2, demonstrating 
the Company’s commitment to integrating environmental considerations into product stewardship and innovation.
	 Energy Efficiency Improvements: Energy audits were conducted in select facilities to identify opportunities for energy 
efficiency, and Energy Management System (EMS) solutions were selectively deployed. Broader use of waste heat recovery 
from air compressors has been implemented, channelling the captured energy into water pre-treatment processes, 
significantly reducing the need for thermal energy. Automatic Power Factor Correction (APFC) panels and IRIS systems for 
enhancing power factor and electrical load distribution were used to reduce energy losses. Initiatives to optimise the usage 
of motor energy were expanded through rightsizing motor power, wider Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs), and upgrades 
to energy-efficient IE4 motors. Key machinery and equipment were upgraded or retrofitted with advanced, energy-efficient 
54  
|Endurance Technologies Limited
=== page 325 ===
components to elevate energy performance at the operational level. Please refer to the ‘Conservation of Energy’ section in 
Annexure I to the Board’s report on Page 96 of the Annual Report for additional measures implemented. 
	 Greening of Supply Chain: For reducing Scope 3 emissions, the Company actively engages with its value chain partners 
through capability-building initiatives, best practice sharing sessions, and targeted interventions to improve environmental 
and regulatory compliance, while continuously monitoring their progress. Currently, 20 partners are part of a sustainability 
index programme that evaluates their performance and monitors improvement across key sustainability parameters. 
The Company has also trained its top suppliers on sustainable practices and BRSR value chain reporting expectations 
and has proactively collected data on GHG emissions and other ESG parameters to drive improvements, ahead of 
compliance requirements.
	 Green Buildings: The new plants at Aurangabad Industrial City (AURIC) Bidkin and AURIC Shendra are being developed 
as planned green building projects, and the same design approach is being adopted, where feasible, for plant expansions. 
Across these projects, key features include site planning that preserves natural contours, daylight-linked design through 
skylights, north-light and transparent roofing sheets, natural ventilation, and high-Solar Reflectance Index (SRI) roof finishes 
to mitigate the heat-island effect. This approach supports lower energy demand and improved environmental performance.
	 Carbon Sequestration through Green Cover: The Company amplified its tree plantation efforts on and around operational 
sites, reinforcing its long-term commitment to capturing carbon and enhancing ecosystem resilience. 
	 Educational Trainings and Industrial Visits: The Company continued to strengthen internal sustainability capabilities 
through focused training and knowledge-sharing initiatives. During the year, two group-level training sessions on 
sustainable manufacturing and a waste management training programme were conducted by the Corporate Sustainability 
Team. Twenty employees were certified as ISO 50001:2018 Lead Auditors by TUV SUD South Asia Pvt. Ltd., while twenty-
five employees were trained as Green Professionals by CII. Industrial visits to facilities, including Godrej & Boyce, Godrej 
Vikhroli and Alfa Laval, were also undertaken to build awareness and understanding of sustainability best practices relating 
to energy efficiency, waste management and sustainable operations.
 For a more comprehensive picture of the Company’s approach towards carbon neutrality, please refer to the “Sustainability” 
section of the Annual Report on Page 52.

10. Briefly describe the waste management practices adopted in your establishments. Describe the strategy adopted by 
your company to reduce the usage of hazardous and toxic chemicals in your products and processes and the practices 
adopted to manage such wastes.
The Company maintains a robust waste management framework aligned with statutory requirements and guided by circular 
economy and life cycle thinking. All manufacturing sites are equipped with compliant waste handling infrastructure, including 
segregated scrap yards, impervious flooring, designated compartments, and fire safety systems. Waste monitoring is carried 
out through physical inspections and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP)- based tracking, while disposal is done via PCB-
authorised vendors. The Company complies with EPR obligations under CPCB guidelines for Plastic, Battery and e-Waste 
categories as detailed in Principle 2 Essential Indicator 4. The Company’s focus on waste management is further emphasised 
through the organisation of monthly campaigns on waste management practices across locations, driving awareness and 
continuous improvement. 
Specific initiatives to reduce hazardous waste generation and minimise the use of toxic chemicals include chrome recovery, nickel 
recovery, thinner recovery, and coolant life-extension through sump and tramp oil cleaning systems. These interventions reduce 
the generation of spent chemicals and waste requiring disposal, enable recovery and reuse of valuable materials, lower the 
consumption of virgin chemicals, and improve compliance and resource efficiency. Waste that cannot be recovered is channelised 
only through authorised recyclers, co-processors or disposal agencies, in line with applicable waste management rules.
The Company applies the 3R principles—Reduce, Reuse, Recycle—across operations. Notable initiatives include aluminium 
scrap recycling, sand reclamation in die-casting, returnable packaging, and the reuse of wooden pallets. Hazardous substance 
use is minimised through a switch to water-based paints, recovery of heavy metals like chrome and nickel, reduction of hazardous 
56  
|Endurance Technologies Limited
=== page 327 ===
material content in brake liners, and moisture reduction in sludge via decanter and volute press systems. E-waste, bio-medical 
waste, and battery waste are managed in accordance with the existing Waste Management Rules and EPR specific to each 
category. The Company continues to advance its ZWTL journey through a structured waste management framework aligned with 
statutory requirements and circular economy principles. In the financial year 2,025–26, 14 plants were awarded the highest level 
ZWTL certification by the certifying bodies, reflecting the Company’s strategic efforts in source segregation, pre-processing of 
foundry and packaging waste, as well as co-processing with cement and energy recovery partners. These actions helped divert 
over 98% of total waste from landfills, also aligning with climate goals by reducing Scope 3 emissions. An organisation-wide 
Waste Management SOP , aligned to DIN SPEC 91,436, has been implemented to standardise segregation, storage, tracking 
and channelisation of waste streams. Key initiatives include greater recycling of metal scrap, coolant recycling, returnable and 
fit-for-purpose packaging, co-processing of eligible waste streams, and ERP-based waste tracking. These actions have improved 
landfill diversion and increased recovery through recycling, reuse and co-processing across sites.
LCAs further support waste reduction planning. As part of its 2030 Sustainability Roadmap, the Company aims to achieve 100% 
landfill diversion and embed waste lifecycle thinking into procurement, design, and operations. Currently, the Company’s landfill 
diversion rate is 98.43%. In Principle 6, Leadership Indicator 6, the Company has also identified potential environmental risks in 
its supplier value chain, particularly around the use of hazardous substances. To address this, it is actively working on embedding 
waste lifecycle thinking into procurement, design, and operations.

5. Does the entity have a business continuity and disaster management plan? Give details in 100 words / web link.
 The Company has established a comprehensive Risk Management Framework as part of its Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) 
approach to identify and manage risks related to natural events, safety, operations, legal compliance, and people, thereby 
supporting business continuity across operations. Each manufacturing plant has designated emergency response teams and 
documented plans covering relevant risk scenarios, which are reviewed periodically, with preparedness measures including 
regular fire and mock drills. Additionally, cross-functional EHS teams, periodic compliance audits, defined safety Key Result 
Areas (KRAs), and access to medical facilities and health check-ups further strengthen resilience and response readiness.
 The Company also conducts bi-annual internal reviews of its Information Security Management System (ISMS), implemented 
across the organisation, with ISO 27001 certification for corporate functions, R&D centres, and select locations. From an 
Information Technology (IT) risk perspective, a structured Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) framework has 
been established as part of the ISO 27001:2022-aligned ISMS to ensure continuity of critical Information Technology (IT services 
during disruptions such as data centre outages, application failures, or cybersecurity incidents. Supported by a formal Risk 
Assessment and Risk Treatment Plan (RARTP), defined recovery priorities, and governance oversight, the framework is further 
strengthened through Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) to restrict unauthorised access, enhanced Security Operations Centre 
(SOC) capabilities for continuous monitoring and rapid threat response, improved hardening of network and operating systems 
to reduce vulnerabilities, and refined incident response and disaster recovery processes to enable faster restoration of operations.

6. Disclose any significant adverse impact to the environment, arising from the value chain of the entity. What mitigation or 
adaptation measures have been taken by the entity in this regard.
 The Company continues to proactively assess and manage environmental risks across its value chain through structured supplier 
engagement, monitoring, and capability-building initiatives. During the reporting period, no significant adverse environmental 
impacts were observed that were not being actively mitigated; however, key risk areas identified across suppliers included 
energy-intensive operations, water consumption, and waste generation.  To address these risks, the Company has implemented 
targeted mitigation and adaptation measures in collaboration with its suppliers:
	 Transition to Cleaner Energy: Suppliers have significantly increased the adoption of renewable energy. A cumulative 14.35 
MW of solar capacity and 12.64 MW of wind energy have been installed across vendor facilities. Certain suppliers have 
achieved or exceeded 100% of their electricity requirements through renewable sources.
	 Energy Efficiency Improvements: Focused interventions such as installation of energy-efficient lighting, optimisation of 
motors and pumps, reduction of machine idle time, and deployment of variable frequency drives (VFDs) have resulted in 
measurable reductions in energy consumption.
	 Water Conservation and Recycling: Suppliers have strengthened water stewardship by recycling through ETP/STP 
systems, rainwater harvesting, and leak-prevention measures, resulting in significant water savings. Continuous monitoring 
and awareness initiatives have further improved water-use efficiency.
	 Afforestation and Carbon Sequestration: Vendor partners have undertaken large-scale plantation drives, with over 
63,000 trees planted, contributing to carbon sequestration and enhancing local biodiversity.
 In addition to compliance verification, the Company actively supports suppliers in addressing identified gaps to ensure alignment 
with consent conditions and regulatory expectations.
7. Percentage of value chain partners (by value of business done with such partners) that were assessed for  
environmental impacts. 
 The Company’s supplier risk assessment evaluates environmental impacts and risk across different categories of suppliers across 
its value chain through a risk-based supplier assessment framework. Suppliers are prioritised based on spend, criticality, and 
environmental risk, and assessed using a Sustainability Index covering policy, compliance, waste, emissions, and management 
systems. Assessments are supported by supplier trainings, site audits, and third-party environmental monitoring, along with 
verification of statutory compliance. for both its OEM and aftermarket suppliers. In addition, for the OEM business, suppliers 
are prioritised based on spend, criticality, and environmental risk, and assessed using a Sustainability Index covering policy, 
compliance, waste, emissions, and management systems. Performance is tracked through periodic reviews and monthly 
management oversight, ensuring continuous improvement and expanding coverage of key value chain partners.
 The direct suppliers (for both the OEM and aftermarket businesses) assessed under this framework collectively account for 66.62% 
of the Company’s total purchases. Another 3.34% of suppliers consist of trading houses and professional service providers whose 
engagements are intermittent in nature and, therefore, are currently outside the scope of assessments, while the remaining 
suppliers form part of the tail-end supplier base and will be progressively assessed in a phased manner.

3. Describe the mechanisms to receive and redress grievances of the community.
 The Company has robust grievance redressal mechanisms to receive and address concerns raised by local communities. To 
facilitate community feedback, suggestion and complaint boxes are placed at the Gram Panchayat offices in villages near the 
Company’s operations. Similar boxes are also available at the WoW (World on Wheels) Bus and the Old Age Day Care Centre. 
Inputs received through these channels are reviewed and prioritised jointly by the Gram Panchayat and Sevak Trust, which serves

established protocols to receive, document, and resolve grievances from neighbouring communities. Issues that require higher-
level intervention are escalated and addressed by the appropriate authority. In addition, the Stakeholder Engagement Policy 
details grievance handling mechanisms by stakeholder type and can be viewed on https://www.endurancegroup.com/wp-

1. Describe the mechanisms in place to receive and respond to consumer complaints and feedback.  
 For the OEM segment, customer complaints are addressed by the plant-level Supplier Quality Assurance (SQA) teams. These 
teams track and resolve complaints through a structured process. The process includes systematic monitoring and regular follow-
ups. This helps ensure timely resolution and supports the Company’s quality and customer satisfaction standards. Customers 
may raise queries related to products or services or register grievances through multiple channels. These include email at 
customercare@endurance.co.in and telephone at 0240-2569723 or +91 8010187593. Concerns may also be submitted in person 
or through the post at the registered office located at E-92, MIDC Industrial Area, Waluj, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar – 431 
136, Maharashtra.
 For the aftermarket segment, the Company follows a structured complaint management process to address concerns raised 
by distributors and dealers. Complaints are received from distributors via email, telephone or engaging with the field force. 
Mechanics and retailers can also raise complaints and service requests through the Company’s Endurance Saathi App. All 
complaints are categorised based on the nature of the issue and assigned a defined Turnaround Time (TAT). They are then 
routed to the relevant internal teams for appropriate action and resolution. The Company monitors complaint resolution to 
ensure concerns are addressed within the stipulated timelines. In addition to the formal complaint management system, the 
Company’s sales force actively engages with distributors and dealers on a regular basis to understand operational challenges, 
gather feedback, and facilitate prompt resolution of concerns. This ongoing interaction strengthens customer relationships 
and helps the Company respond proactively to issues and service requirements, while also supporting effective follow-up and 
closure of concerns.

5. Does the entity have a framework/policy on cybersecurity and risks related to data privacy? (Yes / No) If available, 
provide a web link to the policy.
 The Company operates an enterprise-wide Information Security Management framework aligned with ISO 27001:2022 and 
certified by DNV, covering all locations, functions, employees, and relevant external stakeholders. With independent re-
certification and periodic assessments, the Company has also achieved TISAX Level 3 accreditation. To sustain and further 
strengthen this framework, the Company undertakes periodic internal and external assessments, independent audits, and 
ongoing system enhancements under its ISO 27001-certified framework. Continuous improvement is driven through the timely 
implementation of corrective actions and regular employee awareness programmes, ensuring sustained compliance and a 
proactive approach to data privacy and cyber risk management. It is supported by defined governance structures, periodic 
internal reviews, and surveillance audits to ensure effectiveness. The framework integrates risk assessment, access governance, 
system monitoring, and incident management through a centralised mechanism, including a ticket-based service desk for timely 
resolution and service level adherence. Advanced monitoring tools with real-time alerts are deployed to proactively identify 
and mitigate vulnerabilities and data risks across IT infrastructure, further strengthened by the enablement of ZTNA to restrict 
unauthorised access. This is supported by periodic awareness programmes and accessible policies via the Company’s intranet. 
The policy on IT, Cybersecurity and Data Privacy is available to all internal and relevant external stakeholders. 
 The Company is in the process of implementing the applicable provisions of the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) 
framework as notified by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. A structured roadmap is in place to align 
internal processes, Personally Identifiable Information (PII) data handling practices, and governance protocols with regulatory 
requirements within prescribed timelines. This includes strengthening consent management practices, data classification, access 
controls, and accountability mechanisms to ensure responsible handling and protection of personal data.
6. Provide details of any corrective actions taken or underway on issues relating to advertising, and delivery of essential 
services; cyber security and data privacy of customers; re-occurrence of instances of product recalls; penalty / action 
taken by regulatory authorities on safety of products / services.  
 No corrective action was necessary for advertising delivery of essential services, product recalls or product safety. The Company’s 
cybersecurity and data privacy framework, supported by robust systems, controls, and governance mechanisms, was well 
established and effective before an incident during December 2025. There was no compromise of customer data or breach 
of privacy, and no material impact on business operations, with core applications and critical infrastructure remaining secure 
and affected systems restored within 1–2 days. This demonstrates the strength of the Company’s preventive controls, real-time 
monitoring capabilities, and incident response readiness. The Company also maintains a strong track record in safeguarding 
customer data privacy and cybersecurity, with no complaints reported during the year, reflecting the effectiveness of its structured 
information security framework supported by well-defined policies, robust access controls, continuous monitoring systems, and 
established incident response protocols.
